sentences.text: The scientific name highlights the distinctive long pennaceous feathers located on the metatarsus.
These longest foot feathers measured roughly 55 millimeters, which is just a bit shorter than the leg bone they sit upon.
A second toe possessed an enlarged claw that was slightly shortened and less developed than the sickle-shaped claws found in related species.
Evidence suggests shorter feathers covered the long ones, indicating the presence of coverts similar to those seen in modern birds.
The genus was first described by researchers Xu and Zhang in the year 2005.
Fossil remains were unearthed within the Daohugou Bed of the Tiaojishan Formation in the regions of Hebei and Liaoning, China.
The specific epithet daohugouensis directly references the Daohugou locality where the holotype specimen was discovered.
Pedopenna was likely a carnivore that hunted insects, small reptiles, and mammals.
Xu and Zhang suggested in 2005 that the foot feathers could have served an ornamental function or were vestigial.
Pedopenna is classified within Paraves, the group of maniraptoran dinosaurs that includes birds and their closest relatives.
The parent group for this animal is Paraves.
It is classified under the class Reptilia.
Recent studies have recovered Pedopenna as a scansoriopterygid.
More recently, Pedopenna has been recovered as a scansoriopterygid.
This creature lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 163 million years ago in the Callovian stage, in what is now Asia.
Recent radiometric dating places Pedopenna in the middle Jurassic Callovian, approximately 168 million years ago.
The estimated time range for this taxon spans between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
Pedopenna is possibly older than Archaeopteryx, although the exact age of the Daohugou Beds where it was found is debated.
It is debated whether Pedopenna is as old as Archaeopteryx, depending on the age of the Daohugou Bed.
Xu and Zhang postulated that Asia is the cradle of the origin of birds based on the presence of this basal avian lineage member.
